note: What a webhook receiver can rely on: the envelope, the signature, the events and each content payload's keys. spec/contracts/webhook_contract_spec.rb holds the CMS to it; a change here is a change every receiver sees. See docs/webhooks.md.

webhook.signature_format: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body>
webhook.signature_key: the Webhook's secret: generated by the CMS, or set to the one the receiver issued
webhook.timestamp_format: Unix seconds when the post was signed (each attempt is signed afresh)
webhook.signature_v2_format: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<X-CMS-Timestamp>.<raw request body>">, same key; check it and the timestamp's age (5 minutes is the advised tolerance) to refuse a replayed post
webhook.delivery_is: the delivery's id, the same on every retry of it: a receiver drops one it has already handled
webhook.retries: a delivery that can't connect, times out, or is answered 408, 429 or 5xx is sent again after 30s, 2m, 5m, 15m and 40m (six attempts in all), then given up on; any other answer is final
webhook.tenant_is: the install's site key (SITE_KEY, else the first label of APP_HOST)
webhook.schema_changed_is: sent when /api/v1/schema's digest (meta.schema_digest, the X-CMS-Schema-Digest header) moves: block types, collections, globals or a live page's fields changed. Debounced (writes settle for 2s), and only when the digest actually differs. It also rebuilds or purges the site (cache tag schema), as a content change does.
webhook.url_is: absolute, canonical-aware, and identical to the address the sitemap publishes for the same record (PubliclyAddressable), so a receiver can match a payload to a URL from search or analytics.
webhook.external_id_is: <kind>-<data.id>, e.g. page-12 — CMS ids are unique per type, not across types
